_comment: PLB-1244 golden values for the PJ subsequent-filing flow, on fixture cause 202653957
(CaseSerial 1773097, TAXLIT13 Serial 34).
SOURCE OF THESE VALUES (TESTING_RULES.md rules 1 and 2): every entry below was read out
of fixtures/wire-samples/pj_postfix_20261006.xml - a real outbound ReviewFiling envelope
captured from the deployed TaxLit13PJSubmit.exe - and then independently corroborated:
filer_type 54323          the resolved 'Government Filer' code. 40467 is the
'Not Applicable' hardcode that shipped on every subsequent
filing until 2026-10-01.
filing_attorney           id 22b3f700-... is confirmed independently of the capture by
PICK_LIST('EfileAttorney') where PICK_VALUE='Susan Fuertes',
whose ExtraInfo4 reads 'Firm attorney list: id=22b3f700-...'.
PjConstants.FilingAttorneyName is 'Susan Fuertes', and the
user confirmed 2026-10-05 that Susan is correct for PJ.
Category IDENTIFICATION is the POST-FIX pairing: Tyler echoes
the field back only for this pairing and silently discarded it
for the pre-fix CASEPARTYATTORNEYID pairing.
filing_code 136718        'No Fee Documents' (plural - a near-miss fails code
resolution), PjConstants.FilingCodeName.
filing_description        PjConstants.FilingDescription, verbatim. Deliberately NOT
TAXLIT13.FilingDescription, which on Serial 34 currently reads
'4BTN test - PJ excess proceeds packet'.
document_file_control_id  PjConstants.ClientRefPrefix ('99999902', EIGHT digits) + '-' +
the cause. ECF4's seven-digit '9999902-' is a separate open
question and is not what this flow sends.
file_descriptions         per-file BinaryDescriptionText = each document's file name,
which is what the clerk sees next to the attachment.
filing_party_ids          Harris County's OWN CASEPARTYID on this case - the exact-match
fee-party resolver, not 'the first party', which on a tax suit
is usually the original petitioning taxing entity.
payment_amount 0.00       the 'waiver' payment account.
case_category/case_type   null on a subsequent filing: they are new-case-only fields.
person_names []           PJ declares no parties at all on a subsequent filing.
optional_services []      PJ requests none today. Kept as an explicit empty list so that
PJ gaining one is a visible change, since a service sent with
no Multiplier is ErrorCode 129.
'wire' is fed to harness.wire.compare, which treats it as an ALLOWLIST - adding a key
tightens this test and can never loosen it.

config.Flow.shared_dump) by four independent markers that are all PJ constants: filing
code 136718, DocumentFileControlID '99999902-202653957', the filing description, and PJ's
It is POST-FIX: FilerTypeText is the resolved 54323 and FilingAttorneyID carries

attorney-category fix. It also carries the PLB-1169 e-service block, so it postdates that.
NOT CLAIMED: the envelope number. TAXLIT13 Serial 34 currently holds EnvelopeNum 328529,
and the attach/read-back calls Tyler logged at 14:04 and 14:05 bracket this capture's
14:03 mtime, so 328529 is very probably this envelope - but the ReviewFiling RESPONSE was

date rather than by envelope so nothing downstream treats the inference as evidence.

_comment: The e-service half of PLB-1244. Each required contact below is derivable from today's
LawBase_Design COS data for CaseSerial 1773097 by PjCosServiceContacts' own rule, and
its Tyler id is confirmed by the GetServiceInformationHistory capture in
../service-history/pj_202653957_20261006.xml. That is why these three are asserted and
the capture's fourth contact is not - see unexplained_in_capture below.

required_contacts.name: Angelica Hernandez
required_contacts.why: THE load-bearing case for this ticket. The COS row is the FIRM Linebarger Goggan Blair & Sampson, LLP, whose own CONTACT0 email is houlitigation@lgbs.com - but TAXLIT2.AttyofRec ('100037^496') points at Contact9 Serial 496, the individual attorney Angelica Hernandez, and it is HER address that must be served. A regression that read the firm row instead would still produce a valid-looking lgbs.com address, ErrorCode 0 and a clean DB write, which is exactly why this is pinned to the exact id and the exact address.

required_contacts.name: Perdue, Brandon, Fielder, Collins & Mott, L.L.P.
required_contacts.source: firm email, no attorney of record
required_contacts.why: The contrast that makes the Hernandez assertion meaningful: this COS row has an EMPTY AttyofRec, so there is no Contact9 person to prefer and the firm's own address is correctly what gets served. The two rows together prove the resolver is choosing, not defaulting.

required_contacts.name: Cynthia Willis
required_contacts.why: A pro-se defendant - no attorney of record, ServeCert 'Email', served at her own CONTACT0 address. Her email is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is stand-in test data (a personal address someone put on the Design row so this branch could be exercised at all) and will legitimately change. The regression signal that matters is that a party with no attorney is still e-served from her own contact row, so this entry asserts the id and the source, not the address. Note this is also the row that used to trip the 'NEEDS PUBLIC LIST' block - it no longer does, which is why that block is now asserted ABSENT on this case.

must_not_be_eserved.name: Maria Conception Willis All Unknown Heirs, Successors Or Assigns
must_not_be_eserved.why: On the COS but mail-only. She must appear in the review screen's mail list and must NOT receive a service contact in the envelope. 'ServeCert contains Email' is the rule; hers says USPS Regular only.

unexplained_in_capture.name: Khurram Khwaja
why: OPEN QUESTION, deliberately not asserted either way (TESTING_RULES.md rules 1 and 8).
This contact is in the captured envelope's serve list, but Khwaja is NOT derivable from
CaseSerial 1773097's COS: Contact9 Serial 19912 is not referenced by any TAXLIT2 row on
that case, at any CertofService value. He IS on cause 202017727's COS (Contact9 19912 via
The history capture shows his only action on this case is an Attach at 2026-10-06
19:04:11Z - one minute AFTER this envelope was built - so he was not attached at case
level when the envelope was assembled either. Whether a hand-run --attach-service-contact
during the 10/06 session put him in scope, or Design data has changed since, is not
Because the envelope's contact set therefore cannot be fully explained from current data,
the tests assert that the three required contacts are PRESENT and that the mail-only
party is ABSENT, plus structural properties of the whole list - but never an exact
count or an exact set. Pinning '== 4' would be pinning a value nobody can justify.

db_writeback._comment: PLAN.md's third assertion layer. Read from LawBase_Design 2026-10-15.
envelope_note: EnvelopeNum is asserted as 'present and numeric', never equal to a literal - every new
live send legitimately replaces it. Both values are recorded only so a human can tell
which send the row currently reflects.
328529 was the value before 2026-10-15 and is the one timestamp-correlated to the wire
capture (see capture_evidence). 329145 is a RECORDED FACT rather than an inference: the
submit wrote it back to TAXLIT13A.TylerResponse verbatim as
That 329145 send was the first execution of test_live_submit_matches_golden_and_writes_back,
and it PASSED - ErrorCode 0, the live envelope matched every field in 'wire' above, and the
write-back landed. So all three of PLAN.md's assertion layers are now proven for PJ against a
freshly sent envelope, not only against the committed capture. It was run unintentionally
(`pytest -m tyler` replaces the default marker filter instead of narrowing it, so it selected
the @submits test too); the result stands on its own either way.
